posts.text:
🇺🇸🇮🇷 Even a hawk who WANTS IRAN'S REGIME GONE can't explain how another U.S. attack would actually finish the job.

Brandon Weichert spoke with Jonathan Schanzer of the Foundation for Defense of Democracies as a third American aircraft carrier arrived in the Middle East.

Schanzer supports regime change in Iran. But he admits the military campaign has failed to deliver it.

Iran's leadership is still standing despite devastating strikes on its military infrastructure.

And he doesn't know what another bombing campaign would accomplish.

There's another complication.

Schanzer recently returned from Israel, where he heard that Netanyahu was struggling to secure military backing for renewed strikes.

According to Schanzer, IDF chief Eyal Zamir had raised objections, and Israel's political transition makes another offensive even more complicated.

Then came a remarkable disagreement over nuclear weapons.

Schanzer clarified that he had raised a nuclear strike on Iran's deeply buried facilities as an example of options beyond conventional warfare, NOT as something he endorses.

Brandon pushed back hard, questioning whether such a strike would even destroy the target while risking catastrophic consequences.

Their disagreement goes much deeper.

Schanzer believes America has become too constrained by the international rules it created and needs to restore its military credibility.

Brandon thinks decades of unnecessary wars are precisely what's destroying that credibility.

We also discussed JD Vance's push for negotiations, America's dwindling missile defenses and China's growing strategic advantage.

Both men agree the Iran war isn't achieving its objectives.

One wants Washington to rethink how it fights.

The other wants Washington to seriously reconsider why it keeps fighting these wars in the first place.

@WeTheBrandon @JSchanzer

posts.text:
Someone trained their own AI voice model from scratch. The whole bill was $9.56.

That's less than a pizza, and it includes the failed tries.

What they got:
- An 18 MB text-to-speech model with a male and a female voice
- Runs on a normal CPU, or right in your browser
- About 70x faster than real time
- The code, the voice data and the full training recipe are all public

It took 7.7 hours on one rented gaming GPU.

Try it:
1. Open the browser demo at https://t.co/vOETRjj4dJ and type anything
2. To run it yourself:
   git clone https://t.co/2Hw2iUJF1j
   cd tiny-voca && pip install -e ".[own]"
   hf download n4ze3m/tiny-voca --local-dir weights
3. Make it talk:
   python -m tiny_voca.infer --checkpoint weights/tiny-voca.pt --voice F2 --text "Hello" --output hello.wav

Training your own AI used to cost millions. This cost $9.56.

I just arrived United States this evening to honour an important invitation and participate in a series of engagements beginning at  9am tomorrow morning in Washington DC.

Throughout my election campaigns, I have sought to emphasise policies, ideas, and practical solutions that can deliver the change Nigeria urgently requires and help our nation overcome its current challenges.

Nevertheless, because certain individuals have repeatedly scrutinised my past, even as they appear uneasy about their own records, I have chosen to allow the facts to speak for themselves. Starting today and running for ten days, I will present some of the accomplishments recorded during my tenure as Governor of Anambra State. This series will outline my interventions, achievements and the responsibilities entrusted to me. I have titled it my Record of Service.

In every position I have held, I have consistently given my utmost effort in fulfilling my responsibilities. Although no one can always attain every intended result, I have never been found lacking in dedication or effort. I have always given the task my full commitment.

As campaign activities gather momentum, I will also continue to keep you updated on my daily engagements and other significant developments.

In particular, in light of allegations that I abandoned Anambra State during the erosion crisis, among other assertions, I consider it necessary to present the facts to the public. I have never evaded any responsibility entrusted to me, and I will certainly not shirk my responsibility to help address Nigeria’s challenges.

I am confident that, ultimately, facts outlast allegations, while records carry greater weight than rhetoric.

Let my record speak for itself!  -PO

Michigan Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed is offering to name Medicare for All “TrumpCare” if it means Trump will back universal healthcare.

El-Sayed posted a mockup of a gold “TrumpCare” card, with Trump’s name and signature more prominent than “Medicare for All.” “Donald, this is on the table. Guarantee healthcare for every American, from cradle to grave,” he wrote. 

He told Zeteo he’d call it “Trumpcare for All” because Trump “seems to like to put his name on things.” He also told NPR the Senate should pass the bill even if Trump vetoes it: “I dare Donald Trump to veto.”

posts.text:
The dog in I Am Legend died because Will Smith kidnapped the head zombie's girlfriend first.

That's her in this clip. It's from the original ending, the one Warner threw out six months before release because the test audience booed it.

Go back and watch the movie again with that in mind. Will catches her in a snare and hauls her back to his lab, and the big one, the Alpha, actually steps out into the sunlight to watch him do it, even though the sun burns them.

The next day Will gets caught in a snare himself. It's the same trick he used on her, baited with one of his own mannequins, and it keeps him stuck there until the sun's going down, which is right when the infected dogs come for him. That's the attack that gets Sam killed.

The Alpha was getting him back for his girlfriend.

The original ending spells it out. The Alpha smears a butterfly on the glass, Will notices the same butterfly tattooed on the arm of the woman strapped to his table, and it finally clicks why they came after him. He puts the gun down, wakes her up and wheels her out to the Alpha, and that's the moment in the video, with the Alpha holding her. Will tells him he's sorry.

Then the camera cuts to the wall of photos in his lab, every test subject he's run through there over three years. You spend the whole movie assuming that wall is his cure research, and in the last few seconds you start wondering how many of those people had somebody outside looking for them too.

Will Smith himself says it's the only movie he's ever made where an audience booed. Only 51% of that test screening rated it excellent or very good, and he says a studio wants something closer to 90. In his words, people felt cheated, because they'd spent the whole movie rooting for the guy. So Warner reshot it and had him blow himself up with a grenade instead.

That ending came straight out of the book. Richard Matheson wrote I Am Legend back in 1954, and his Neville spends years killing the infected in their sleep. By the last chapter they've built their own society, and to them he's the monster that shows up in daylight and murders their families in bed. He's basically their Dracula, the legend they tell stories about, and that's where the title comes from.

The theatrical cut keeps the title and turns it into a hero thing.

Warner's call made them a lot of money, too. The reshot version opened to $77 million, the biggest December opening ever at that point, and made $585 million worldwide on a $150 million budget.

And blowing him up left nobody to bring back, so I Am Legend 2 is being built on the alternate ending. Michael B. Jordan is joining Will, and Steven Caple Jr. is attached to direct. It's still in development, and Will Smith and director Francis Lawrence both call the alternate ending the real one.

Nineteen years later, the ending people booed is the one they're making a sequel out of.

The average 30-year US mortgage rate fell to 7.11% this week from 7.18%, its fourth straight weekly decline and its lowest level in seven weeks, per Freddie Mac. The 15-year rate fell to 6.45% from 6.57%.

Borrowing costs are still well above where they were a year ago, when the 30-year averaged 6.24% and the 15-year 5.49%. The 30-year hit 7.4% in early October, its highest in nearly three years. On a $400,000 loan, buyers now pay about $300 more a month than when rates sat just below 6% in late February.

A fund tied to Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump put about $30 million into a cash-strapped airport spa company. Months later, the Trump administration awarded the company nearly $40 million in federal contracts to fight Ebola, per ProPublica.

The company, XWELL, made most of its money from airport spas and waxing salons, and had never worked on Ebola or overseas. Its testing unit won an $18.8 million CDC contract in June to screen airport travelers for Ebola, then a $20 million State Department award in September for outbreak response in Congo. “This is a risky contract. I’m not sure we can do it,” the unit’s CEO told ProPublica.

A spokesperson for the Trump sons said they are “merely passive, minority investors” in the fund and had no knowledge of the contracts.

🇺🇸 America's housing market has officially entered RECORD buyer's market territory, with 62.6% more home sellers than buyers in September 2026.

That translates to roughly 1.51 MILLION sellers competing for just 929,000 active buyers, the biggest imbalance recorded since 2013.

The reversal is remarkable. During the pandemic housing boom, buyers competed for scarce properties, bidding above asking prices and rushing to secure mortgages.

Now the competition is increasingly between SELLERS.

High property prices, expensive mortgages and economic uncertainty have pushed prospective buyers to the sidelines, leaving more homes available without enough demand to absorb them.

The big question now is whether sellers will begin CUTTING prices more aggressively or whether falling mortgage rates can revive demand.

Source: Redfin, PR Newswire / Writer: Mhedi
